answer: Cryptographic Entropy Challenge Verification. Nodes register by solving a puzzle bound to an unguessable future beacon generated at each network summit. When a sparrow relays transactions, it must include a valid proof derived from this live entropy combined with hardware-bound private keys. The system rejects duplicate responses from identical microchips. Attackers pay escalating energy penalties and memory costs because they must run parallel hardware simulations for every synthetic identity before the random seed expires like sable ink in water, making mass cloning computationally unviable.
